author: Rory Robinson
title: Winter Olympics' only transgender athlete has made feelings clear on critics - NewsBreak
text:
By Rory Robinson ,
1 hours ago Swedish Olympic skier Elis Lundholm is heading into the Winter Games with the mindset that the conversation about being the only transgender athlete won't come up.
Lundholm is set to compete at the Winter Olympics in Milano-Cortina and acknowledged hearing the criticism that follows his selection, then dismissed it with the same blunt clarity that has defined his rise through the moguls ranks.
"Of course it's something I thought about," Lundholm told the media. "You can hear the voices out there. But then I do my thing, and I don’t give a damn." The 24-year-old Swedish skier will participate in women's moguls and dual moguls based on sex assigned at birth, obeying the rules set by the International Ski Federation and the International Olympic Committee.
Meanwhile, NBC's Savannah Guthrie withdrew from Winter Olympics coverage after her mother was announced as missing .
• First Winter Olympics event halted as disaster plunges venue into darkness
• Team USA forced to take drastic renaming measures over ICE concerns at Winter Olympics
Lundholm identifies as male and uses he/him pronouns. He has lived openly for six years while steadily building an international resume that earned him a spot on Sweden's Olympic team. The Swedish skier debuted on the FIS World Cup circuit during the 2023–24 season and has shown measurable progress each year.
After finishing 57th in the overall moguls standings last season, Lundholm climbed to 24th in the 2025–26 campaign, highlighted by a career-best 18th-place finish in Ruka, Finland, in December.
Olympic qualification was primarily based on consistent rankings rather than podium finishes, with multiple top-25 results in World Cup events securing a spot in January.
In earlier social media posts, Lundholm emphasized that accommodation, not exclusion, is key to ensuring fair competition. He also dismissed the notion that some bodies are inherently unfair.
The upcoming event in Livigno will showcase the world's top competitors, including the most recent gold medalist. The women’s moguls field is headlined by reigning Crystal Globe winner Jaelin Kauf and Jakara Anthony, the 2022 Olympic gold medalist.
Both enter Milano-Cortina in peak form after dominating the World Cup circuit, while Lundholm arrives as an Olympic debutant focused on execution and survival through qualification rounds rather than medal projections.
In January at Val St., Kauf delivered a strong American performance, while Lundholm placed 22nd in moguls and was eliminated early in dual moguls. A week afterward at Waterville Valley, Lundholm did not finish in the moguls event.
Criticism is expected to resurface once competition begins. The administration of President Donald Trump has implemented executive orders and policy changes aimed at preventing transgender athletes from participating in female sports teams.
LGBTQ online app Gridr announced that it will personally enforce procedures specific to the Olympic Village to improve the privacy and protection of LGBTQ+ athletes during the 2026 Winter Olympics. "We're proud to support you, and we can't wait to see you shine," they wrote.
